newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: SOCCER-YUGOSLAVIA AT FULL STRENGTH FOR SPAIN CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-YUGOSLAVIA AT FULL STRENGTH FOR SPAIN CLASH.

text.p: Yugoslavia have shaken off all their major injury worries ahead of their top-of-the-table World Cup qualifier against Spain on Wednesday.
"After several days of uncertainty and medical treatment Dejan Savicevic, Branko Brnovic, Sinisa Mihajlovic, Risto Vidakovic, Zoran Mirkovic are in full health," coach Slobodan Santrac said.
"Dejan Savicevic is fully fit and we are happy about this as well as about the successful recovery of all the other players in the squad."
But Drazen Bolic of Partizan Belgrade misses out and will be replaced by Zeljko Petrovic of PSV Eindhoven. Petrovic was due to arrive in Belgrade on Tuesday.
Spanish manager Javier Clemente hopes to have Barcelona defender Sergi Barjuan fit to play in Spain's biggest match of the campaign so far.

Sergi broke a bone in his arm in a Spanish Cup match nearly a month ago but is likely to play on the left side of defence, while Atletico Madrid utility man Juan Lopez is seen as the favourite to take the right side.
Lopez, who has started only seven club games this season, was a surprise choice when named by Clemente but has impressed the Spanish manager in practice sessions.
Real Madrid central defender Rafael Alkorta is also expected to play after shaking off back pains.

"The decision about who finishes first and who finishes second in our group will be made in Belgrade," Clemente said. "We are in a better position...but you know me. I don't like to waste conventional words because they mean little and it is not my habit to talk about tactics."
